name: Axiom
tagline: Managed event and telemetry store with schema-on-read ingest and the piped APL query language.
description: Axiom is a fully managed platform for logs, traces, metrics and other event data, built on its own event store that keeps compressed data on object storage and separates ingest from query compute. Data is ingested without a schema and shaped at read time with APL, a piped query language modelled on Kusto, while a companion language, MPL, targets a dedicated metrics engine. It supports OpenTelemetry and common shippers, offers dashboards, monitors and an MCP server for AI agents, and prices by usage with a free personal tier and a bring-your-own-cloud option. It suits teams that want cheap retention of high-volume telemetry without operating a cluster; it is closed source and cloud-only.

pricing.notes: Free personal plan; paid plans bill ingest, query compute and storage; BYOC available for large customers.

scale.notes: Ingest and query are separate serverless tiers over object storage.

strengths: No cluster to operate; ingest scales without capacity planning
Schema-on-read means new fields need no migrations
APL is expressive for piped log and event analysis
Low storage cost for long retention of high-volume telemetry
Free tier generous enough for side projects
weaknesses: APL and MPL are proprietary query languages
Usage-based pricing needs monitoring at very high query volume
Smaller integration catalogue than Datadog or Splunk
